junction.name: Minnesota Avenue Southeast & 25th Street Southeast, Washington DC

claims.text: Minnesota Avenue Southeast & 25th Street Southeast had 64 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 3 pedestrians injured, 3 cyclists injured and 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $4.4 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.

This corner got Leading Pedestrian Interval signals in 2022. Across the city: at 267 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-19%, 95% interval -35% to +1%) could be zero. Repeating it here is not supported by the city's own record.
The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: not shown (at 267 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-19%, 95% interval -35% to +1%) could be zero).
Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 3.5 crashes a year (CMF 4215, the median of 4 eligible records), worth $1.2 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.9 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites), worth $657,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

The District Department of Transportation (DDOT) is responsible for 25th Street Southeast, Minnesota Avenue Southeast, Palmer Place Southeast, Pennsylvania Avenue Southeast (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the District Department of Transportation (DDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
